docs.text: My favorite artist in the abstract work has to be Vasily Kandinsky. He first pursued figurative art before 1913, he was among the first (if not the first) painters to push into pure abstraction—or as he put it, “art independent of one’s observations of the external world.” He especially believed that color could be separated from all external references and become a subject for art. His 1910 book, "On the Spiritual In Art,” laid out his theories, and became one of the Ur texts of 20th-century Modernism.

When it comes to heat protectants with keratin, there are quite a few options. It's great that you're looking into keratin-infused products as keratin helps strengthen and repair hair, especially with heat styling. For specific product recommendations, I suggest looking for reputable brands that specialize in hair care, as they often have well-researched formulas. Checking reviews, especially from people with similar hair types, can also be helpful.
The frequency of using keratin products depends on your hair type and condition. If you have damaged or color-treated hair, you might benefit from more frequent use. However, for normal hair, using a keratin heat protectant each time you apply heat can be sufficient. It's important to maintain a balance, as too much keratin can make hair stiff and brittle. If you notice your hair feeling hard or less elastic, it might be good to reduce the frequency. Consider alternating between keratin and non-keratin heat protectants to maintain balance.

The main thing that helped boosted my confidence and ego to new heights is simply this: Keeping my word to myself.
I can almost guarantee that the way you are feeling now is because you are not keeping your promises to yourself. You say you'd wake up a certain time but you don't. You'd say you go to the gym but you don't. You'd say you do something meaningful but you don't.

These are my tips and tricks I have been using for a while now:
Cold, cool, or lukewarm showers are the best; they don't dry out your skin and actually can leave it refreshed. Also, this is great for your hair to make it shiny and silky.
If you wear makeup, WASH IT OFF EVERY NIGHT. No exceptions to this one.
Instead of lotion, I use liquid coconut oil to moisturize after a shower. It has helped my KP more than any dermatologist, keeps it silky smooth and touchable, moisturizes like mad, and leaves a light sweet scent. If you can't find coconut oil, look for tubs of Eucerin. It is sent from the skin gods, though expensive.
For a face scrub since I have dry skin, I mix raw sugar with coconut oil and a bit of honey. Rinse and pat dry with a clean towel. I don't know if I'd suggest this for someone with oily skin, though.
Something a lot of people don't do because of the extra time it takes is PAT DRY with a dry towel after you step out of the shower. Rubbing can scrape your skin in ways it shouldn't be. Within 3 minutes of patting dry, apply moisturizer all over. The moisturizer locks in the water on the outer layers of your skin; it doesn't normally put more in. After about three minutes, all that good ole' H2O evaporates.

I have also done Model United Nations for many years. I don’t know if you have heard about it. Each school gets assigned one or more countries. Each student on that school's team is assigned a country and then a committee, which could be the Security Council, UNICEF, trade and development, refugees, economic and financial, environmental, etc.
For example, our high school got Bulgaria and Ethiopia, and I was assigned Bulgaria and the economic and financial committee. In college, I got Poland and an international trade committee.
You study about your country and its policies, and you are also given a set of issues that your committee will discuss. I remember one of our issues in the high school conference was the brain drain of educated and skilled workers in poor countries moving to rich countries.
Then you go to the Model UN conference, usually held in a hotel. You attend sessions with your committee, and they are patterned after the real UN and use the same rules.

To resolve this, I joined a nuclear pact alongside the US, Russia, Senegal, and Sweden to forcibly take the world's uranium supply and store it in a Death Star-esque satellite that would orbit the Earth. Each supporting country had one representative on this space station.
At this same conference, Kazakhstan had been pretty uppity the whole time and people were starting to get a little annoyed. These are my Holy Grails:
Olive oil. I do a warm olive oil mask on my hair at least once per month and have done so for the last 10 years. People always ask me what’s my secret because my hair looks waaay “healthier” than it should. When I tell them olive oil masks, I almost always lose them right there. The next thing they universally say? “What about coconut oil?!” UGH. Coconut oil gets on my nerves. Yes, it’s colorless, smells great, and is so damn trendy you feel like you fit in just by using it. But when it became a huge deal several years ago, I decided to give it a go… And I hated the results. My hair felt stiff and sticky, not at all soft like how my olive oil masks turn out. So ever since I’ve been on a crusade against it. If you want my step-by-step olive oil mask routine, PM me and I’ll copy/paste it from my notes.
Olaplex. I was the BIGGEST skeptic of Olaplex. I didn’t even try it until January of 2018 when I had gotten a shadow root, hated it, and my stylist (love her so much) had to do some crazy stuff to bleach it out. She convinced me to try Olaplex and my hair LOVED it! It’s the best thing to happen to blondes since toner. Imagine the bleaching process is a home invasion robber who kicks your hair’s front door in. Olaplex comes along, shuts the door, and sweeps the porch. I’m very against the term “miracle” product; it’s not magic. It’s technology called a bond builder, which repairs the broken bonds from bleaching, coloring, heat, etc. It instantly makes the hair stronger, softer, and smoother. Don’t overdo it—once or twice a month is fine. Olaplex No. 3 is the take home version that you’d use. Apply to damp hair, let it sit for 20-30 minutes, then shampoo and condition afterwards (very important).

Greek cuisine is known for its delicious and flavorful dishes! One of the classics is moussaka, a hearty casserole made with layers of eggplant, ground meat (usually beef or lamb), tomatoes, and béchamel sauce. It's a comforting and satisfying dish with a rich taste.
Another popular Greek dish is souvlaki, which consists of skewered and grilled pieces of marinated meat (often pork, chicken, or lamb) served with pita bread and various toppings like tomatoes, onions, and tzatziki sauce. It's a great choice for a quick and tasty meal.
If you're a fan of seafood, you might enjoy trying Greek-style grilled octopus or a traditional Greek salad with feta cheese, olives, cucumbers, and tomatoes drizzled with olive oil and oregano. These dishes showcase the fresh and vibrant flavors of Mediterranean cuisine.

docs.text:
I'm sorry to hear that you're going through a tough time, Bella. Breakups can be really difficult, especially when distance is a factor. Here are some tips that might help you cope with the breakup and start feeling better:
1. Allow yourself to grieve: It's perfectly normal to feel sad, angry, or even numb after a breakup. Give yourself permission to experience these emotions and understand that it's a natural part of the healing process.
2. ⁠Lean on your support system: Reach out to friends and family who can offer you emotional support and a listening ear. Talking about your feelings can be cathartic and help you process what you're going through.
3. ⁠Focus on self-care: Take care of your physical and emotional well-being. Make sure to eat healthily, get enough rest, and engage in activities that make you happy and relaxed. Exercise can also be a great way to boost your mood.
4. ⁠Avoid contact with your ex: While it can be tempting to stay in touch with your ex, especially if you were friends before the relationship, it's usually best to have some space to heal and gain perspective. Consider unfollowing or muting them on social media for a while.
5. ⁠Set new goals and routines: This is an opportunity to rediscover yourself and your interests. Set new goals, whether they are personal or professional, and create routines that help you stay focused and motivated.
6. ⁠Seek professional help if needed: If you find that your emotions are overwhelming and affecting your daily life for an extended period, consider speaking to a therapist or counselor who can provide guidance and support.
7. ⁠Time heals: Remember that healing takes time, and it's okay to have ups and downs. Be patient with yourself and allow yourself to gradually move forward.
8. ⁠Consider journaling: Writing down your thoughts and feelings in a journal can be a therapeutic way to process your emotions and gain clarity about the situation.

Here's a simple recipe for chocolate lava cake:
Ingredients:
4 oz (115g) semi-sweet chocolate
1/2 cup (115g) unsalted butter
1 cup (200g) powdered sugar
2 large eggs
2 egg yolks
1 tsp vanilla extract
1/4 cup (30g) all-purpose flour
A pinch of salt
Instructions:
Preheat your oven to 425°F. Grease and flour four ramekins or small oven-safe cups.
In a microwave-safe bowl, melt the chocolate and butter together in 20-30 second intervals, stirring each time, until smooth and well combined.
Stir in the powdered sugar until it's fully incorporated into the chocolate mixture.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the eggs, egg yolks, and vanilla extract until well combined.
Slowly add the egg mixture into the chocolate mixture, stirring until smooth.
Finally, fold in the all-purpose flour and a pinch of salt until just combined.
Divide the batter evenly among the prepared ramekins.
Place the ramekins on a baking sheet and bake in the preheated oven for 12-14 minutes, or until the edges are set but the centers are still soft.
Carefully remove the ramekins from the oven (they'll be hot!) and let them cool for a minute or two.
Run a knife around the edges to loosen the cakes, then invert them onto serving plates.
You can dust them with powdered sugar or top with a scoop of vanilla ice cream for an extra treat. Serve immediately and enjoy the gooey, chocolatey goodness!

docs.text:
My all-time favorite dessert has to be tiramisu, and I'd be thrilled to share the recipe with you. Tiramisu is a classic Italian delicacy that combines layers of coffee-soaked ladyfingers, rich mascarpone cheese, and a dusting of cocoa powder. The result is a heavenly, creamy, and indulgent dessert that's perfect for special occasions or when you're simply craving a sweet treat.
Here's the recipe:
Ingredients:
6 large egg yolks
3/4 cup granulated sugar
1 cup mascarpone cheese
1 1/2 cups strong brewed coffee, cooled
1/4 cup coffee liqueur (optional)
24-30 ladyfingers
Unsweetened cocoa powder, for dusting
Dark chocolate shavings (optional)
Instructions:
In a heatproof bowl, whisk together the egg yolks and granulated sugar until the mixture becomes pale and slightly thickened. This step can be done over a double boiler or using a heatproof bowl placed over simmering water.
Remove the bowl from heat and let it cool for a few minutes. Then, add the mascarpone cheese and mix until smooth and well combined.
In a separate shallow dish, combine the cooled brewed coffee and coffee liqueur if using.
Quickly dip each ladyfinger into the coffee mixture, making sure not to soak them for too long, as they can become too soggy. Arrange a layer of dipped ladyfingers in the bottom of your serving dish.
Spread half of the mascarpone mixture over the ladyfingers, creating an even layer.
Add another layer of dipped ladyfingers on top of the mascarpone layer.
Finish with the remaining mascarpone mixture, smoothing it out with a spatula.
Cover and refrigerate the tiramisu for at least 4 hours or overnight to allow the flavors to meld and the dessert to set.
Before serving, dust the top with unsweetened cocoa powder and garnish with dark chocolate shavings if desired.
Slice and serve your homemade tiramisu to enjoy this classic Italian delight!
Tiramisu is a dessert that never fails to impress, and it's perfect for sharing with friends and family. I hope you give it a try and savor every delightful bite!

docs.text:
I feel like you have to give an ultimatum; either a pay raise to match a competitors offer (lie and say you were offered more money at a different position) or quit.
Realistically you shouldnt quit though so I would continue looking for careers while at work, preferrably one with better benefits (more 401k match, health benefits, higher pay, unlimited PTO, etc.)
A large % of people get pay raises not by staying in a company, but by stating their previous work experience and how efficiently they worked whether it be through projects or referrals.
Your employer is not your friend; they see you are doing extra work and dont want to reward you since you're already doing it at no extra pay; they don't respect you.
Bottom line is give them the ultimatum, but if you want a pay raise and they wont give you one, you will likely find it at a new job. Its much easier for companies to justify hiring VS pay raises as well, because pay raises dont necessarily change how a company works, but hiring someone new does
